identity.name: Nautilus
identity.one_liner: The 1976 original: Genta's porthole Nautilus, a 42mm steel watch priced like gold.

narrative.story: Gerald Genta sketched the Nautilus during a Basel fair lunch, borrowing the proportions of a ship's porthole: a two-part case sealed by lateral 'ears', an embossed horizontal-relief dial, an integrated bracelet. Patek launched it in 1976 as the 3700/1, a 42mm steel watch priced against gold dress watches — the second act of the Genta steel-luxury idea after the Royal Oak. The 28-255 C inside is the same ultra-thin JLC 920 base AP used in the 5402. Production ran, with bracelet revisions, until about 1990.
narrative.collector_notes: Early first-series examples with correct dials and unstretched original bracelets carry the money; service dials and swapped clasps are common after five decades. The market corrected sharply after 2022 — recent New York results sit far below what identical watches asked at the peak.
